text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV-1 detected -> traffic_blackhole on dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-dedicated-3' affecting customer 'paytle-prod'. Router reports >5k rps with 30-40% 503/timeout. Smart-routing shows repeated region fallback attempts. Paging eng-runtime oncall.

alex_oncall: oncall alex here, pulling up dashboards. thanks for the ping. linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panelId=router_error_rate&pool=eu-west-2-dedicated-3

maria_runtime: I can see the spike. Router's capacity_signal for that pool drops to 0 intermittently while node-level GPU metrics are normal. Autoscaler didn't intervene - looks like router decided pool was unhealthy and started rerouting -> fallback loop.

dan_sre: @maria_runtime can you dump the router policy decision trace for a sample request? I want to see which model variant it tried and why fallback kept happening.

maria_runtime: grabbing trace now, here's an anonymized snippet:
```
Routing decision: customer=paytle-prod, route=dedicated, pool=eu-west-2-dedicated-3
Selected model_variant=gpt-open-quant-v1
RPC -> model-server returns 404 VariantNotFound
Router: try region fallback -> choose eu-west-1-dedicated-2
eu-west-1 also attempts gpt-open-quant-v1 -> 404
Router loops through fallback tiers, eventual policy backoff yields 503 to client
```

alex_oncall: 404 for variant is a red flag. Could be wrong model tag in policy or mis-synced model on dedicated pool. @maria_runtime can you check model manifest on the pool?

maria_runtime: checked. Pool image has `gpt-open-quant-v2` only. The routing policy for paytle-prod points at `gpt-open-quant-v1` (old). So router tries v1, gets not found, then triggers fallback across regions trying same variant. That explains the loop.

olivia_prod: tagging product/CS: paytle-prod shows elevated errors and some customers reported timeouts. @jason_support please assemble a quick customer impact note.

jason_support: Starting a short post to customers: "We've detected routing failures for some requests to paytle-prod; engineering has applied mitigations and is investigating root cause. We'll follow up with full details." Will send in ~10m.

dan_sre: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop router from routing to the dedicated pool for paytle-prod (route to hosted fallback only) 2) sync/patch dedicated pool to serve v1 or update policy to v2 3) fix autoscaler metric source to avoid false capacity signals.

alex_oncall: I'll flip the temporary override: disable_dedicated route for paytle-prod. Doing via control-plane API now.

alex_oncall: `curl -X POST "https://control-plane.redwood/api/v1/routing/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"customer":"paytle-prod","disable_dedicated":true,"reason":"incident-1768005123"}'`

infra-bot: control-plane: override applied by alex_oncall. routing_override_id=ovr-20260305-71. All traffic for paytle-prod will now prefer hosted variants.

maria_runtime: Confirming error rate drops back to baseline for paytle-prod after override. Hosted route capacity comfortably handles overflow.

dan_sre: Next: we need to correct the policy or pool. Which do we want? quick fix is patch policy to reference v2. Longer fix is ensure pools run both variants or the model manifest is validated during rollout.

maria_runtime: I'll update the routing policy to point at `gpt-open-quant-v2` for paytle-prod and run a canary. Command: `redwoodctl policy set --customer paytle-prod --model-variant gpt-open-quant-v2 --confirm`

maria_runtime: policy update pushed. Running canary test: `curl -H "x-customer: paytle-prod" https://api.redwood/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'` -> 200 OK from hosted. Will test dedicated when we re-enable.

alex_oncall: while this is good, we still saw router capacity_signal flips earlier — could that be autoscaler probe confusion that caused premature blackholing?

dan_sre: I instrumented the autoscaler logs. It uses `ready_process_count` from the runtime agent. During a health rolling update last night, that metric temporally returned 0 for short windows (agent restarted) and router interpreted as capacity=0, started rerouting. Because the policy referenced missing variant, fallback loop ensued. Root cause: two unrelated things colliding (model variant mismatch + flaky readiness metric).

olivia_prod: Customer impact summary for Incident Commander: paytle-prod experienced ~12 minutes of elevated 5xxs and timeouts for ~4% of requests before routed to hosted fallback. No data exfiltration.

jason_support: Sent customer note: "Mitigation applied; we've rerouted traffic and are updating configs. We'll follow up with RCA and ETA for full restore to dedicated routing."

maria_runtime: Next step: validate pool model manifests and add policy linting to CI. Also adding a router guard: if variant returns VariantNotFound, don't immediately try region fallback for the same variant — treat as policy error and fail fast to avoid loop.

dan_sre: I'll push a hotfix to the router decision logic: if error == VariantNotFound then mark policy_error and stop cross-region fallback for that request. Patch PR: `github.com/redwood/router/pull/492` (testing in canary).

alex_oncall: autoscaler fix: switch from `ready_process_count` to `active_inflight_connections` as primary capacity signal (monotonic and not reset on agent restart). I'll schedule a rolling deploy of autoscaler config.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by dan_sre: router-hotfix to canary cluster. CI passed: e2e routing tests OK.

maria_runtime: After policy update + override, and router guard in canary, I'm seeing stable behavior. Planning to re-enable dedicated routing for paytle-prod at T+40m if green.

alex_oncall: Re-enable dedicated routing now (manual step) in 5m window. Doing a small traffic split 90% hosted / 10% dedicated to observe.

infra-bot: routing_override ovr-20260305-71 removed by alex_oncall. traffic_split: hosted=90,dedicated=10.

maria_runtime: 10% to dedicated looks fine; dedicated serving v2 responds 200. Gradually ramping to 50/50. No 404s.

olivia_prod: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-032-17 with summary + customer impact + timeline + mitigations + follow-ups.

dan_sre: Post-incident actions: 1) add policy lint that catches variant not found (CI) 2) change autoscaler metric to active_inflight_connections 3) ensure pool model manifests contain listed variants or fail deploy 4) add dashboard alert for sudden ready_process_count drops.

alex_oncall: Marking incident as RESOLVED -> mitigation in place, routing restored to dedicated, controllers patched. Will add retros later.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: incident_id=1768005123, severity=SEV-1, duration=00:18:07. Summary: Variant mismatch + readiness metric flaps caused router to misread capacity -> fallback loop -> traffic blackholing. Mitigations: routing override, policy update to v2, router guard PR, autoscaler metric change.

maria_runtime: I'll draft the RCA and share in #postmortems. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :tada:
